# A sensor network for Kandy: what to buy, where to put it, and what it would settle

**Drafted 2026-09-05, revised the same day to stratify on flow physics as well as emissions.** Design generated by `scripts/design_sensor_network.py`, scored against alternatives by
`scripts/design_comparison.py`, receptor layer by `scripts/pull_kandy_receptors.py`. Figures:
`plot_sensor_design.py`, `plot_design_justification.py`. Candidate coordinates in
`data/processed/decomp/sensor_design_kandy.csv`. Folded into the thesis as section 9.7.

---

## 1. What this campaign is for, and what it is not for

**It is not for building a validated one kilometre map.** This project has measured, six times,
that within-city spatial pattern is not recoverable from globally available covariates, once with
a detection limit fixed in advance. It has also measured that a tenfold refinement of the grid
moves the paired-site ratio by essentially nothing. A campaign sold as "we will now make the map
finer" would be spending money against a result this project already has.

**It is for four things the existing evidence says are worth measuring**, in descending order of
how well the evidence supports them:

1. **Anchoring the level.** Of four independent Kandy point records, three sit below the model
   and one matches, and the one that matches has an undocumented instrument. This is an open
   discrepancy on the axis the project calls strong, and one reference-grade instrument closes
   it.
2. **Measuring the within-cell distribution.** Chapter 8 argues this is the well-posed quantity,
   the larger of the two, and unreported by any gridded product. Nothing but paired microsites
   can measure it.
3. **Testing the flow physics the model imposes and has never validated**, meaning the nocturnal
   drainage sink it predicts down-valley of the core, and the confinement term. ⚠ This item
   replaced an earlier one, "testing whether the spatial ceiling is a sampling artefact", which
   **did not survive its own power calculation**. Section 6 gives the numbers.
4. **Establishing what susceptible people actually breathe**, which is a different question from
   what a map says and is answered at different locations.

---

## 2. The three measurements that determine the design

**The design space is enormous and the present network samples almost none of it.** Across the
15 by 15 km domain the fine emission surface spans **65 times** from its 10th to its 90th
percentile at 94 m resolution. The existing fixed records sit between the **61st and 100th
percentile** of that range. The entire lower 61 per cent is unsampled, and one of the two
low-cost sensors is **outside the domain altogether**. A network cannot recover a gradient it
never straddles, and this one never straddles it.

**The microscale signal is real, large and local.** A 25-site survey inside the city recorded
concentrations falling from 110 to 4 micrograms per cubic metre over 300 metres, with an
R-squared of 0.82 against traffic intensity. Two of its sites, 300 metres apart inside one model
cell, differ by a factor of 27.5 observationally while the model returns exactly unity. The
decay length is tens to hundreds of metres.

**Susceptible people are concentrated where the model is least trustworthy.** Of 150 mapped
schools, health facilities and care institutions in the domain, **78 (52 per cent) sit above the
90th percentile of the emission surface**, and the median school sits at the 91st. That is a
statement about a proxy rather than a measurement, which is exactly the point: the receptors are
where the model's least validated axis matters most.

---

## 3. The design: 35 sites in five strata

Strata are kept separate because they answer different questions, and because **a site used to
fit a model cannot honestly validate it.**

| stratum | n | instrument | purpose |
|---|---:|---|---|
| **A. Anchor** | 1 | reference-grade | calibrates everything else; settles the level discrepancy |
| **B. Design** | 12 | low-cost | spans emission AND flow physics; the model-information stratum |
| **C. Paired** | 9 | low-cost | triplets inside single cells; the within-cell distribution |
| **E. Vertical** | 5 | low-cost | floor-to-ridge transect; the axis no network samples |
| **D. Receptor** | 8 | low-cost | schools and clinics; exposure, **held out of fitting** |

### The design samples the physics, not only the sources

A design stratified on emissions alone samples where the sources are and learns nothing about
what the atmosphere does with them. The design stratum spans seven covariates: emission
intensity and population for the human footprint, and height above the local valley floor, depth
below the surrounding terrain, nocturnal ventilation, nocturnal flow convergence and the
day-to-night ventilation ratio for the atmosphere.

**Nocturnal drainage.** Cold air runs downslope after sunset and pools. The diagnostic wind field
varies threefold in nocturnal speed across the domain, and its convergence marks the sinks where
that air accumulates. The model predicts one down-valley of the core and no instrument has tested
it.

**Confinement.** Depth below the surrounding terrain is what traps a nocturnal inversion, and the
model's confinement term is built from it and has never been validated.

⚠ **Sky view factor was measured and then dropped.** It is the natural covariate for the
radiative cooling that forms an inversion, but on this domain its coefficient of variation is
0.023 and its interquartile range is 0.021 on a 0 to 1 scale, because the ridges that would
occlude the sky sit 5 to 10 km away. A near-constant covariate in a conditioned Latin hypercube
consumes an optimiser dimension and dilutes the ones that carry contrast.

**The vertical gradient, which is the axis nobody samples.** Monitored stations worldwide sit on
the valley floor, which is why this project's dynamic-transport diagnostic could not be
interpreted. Kandy has 846 m of relief inside the domain and the transect spans
8 to 291 m above the local valley floor.

### Logistics is a constraint, never an objective

Only **19,467 of 25,600 cells** (76 per cent) lie within
400 m of a mapped road and are therefore serviceable. Candidates outside that
set are removed **before** the design is optimised. Making access an objective rather than a
constraint is exactly how convenience sampling happens.

### Why these sites and not the obvious alternatives

Five designs were built on the same candidate grid with the same covariates and scored on the
same measures.

| design | relative D-efficiency | gradient covered | representativeness (lower better) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| D-optimal | 1.00 | 90 | 0.344 |
| existing network | 0.88 | 37 | 0.556 |
| road-sited, the convention | 0.70 | **1** | 0.509 |
| hybrid | 0.48 | 78 | 0.205 |
| random draw | 0.42 | -- | 0.238 |
| **proposed (cLHS)** | 0.35 | **94** | **0.127** |
| population-weighted | 0.31 | 52 | 0.396 |

🔴 **The textbook criterion ranks the two known-failing designs highest.** D-efficiency rates the
conventionally road-sited network at 0.70 and the existing
Kandy network at 0.88, against
0.35 for the proposed design. The road-sited design earns that while
sampling **1 percentile** of the emission gradient,
because D-efficiency rewards spread on the other covariates and is indifferent to collapse on the
one that matters.

⚠ **The cost is real.** The proposed design gives up
65 per cent of D-efficiency, which puts it below a random
draw on that measure alone. The justification is not that the criterion is wrong in general. It
is that D-efficiency is defined relative to an assumed model, this project has six nulls
recording that assumption failing, and the campaign exists to test whether better sampling
rescues it. Buying coefficient precision for a model that does not work is buying the wrong
thing.

🟢 **The site count is set by saturation, not budget.** Beyond 12 design
sites a further site improves representativeness by less than 0.01, averaged over five random
restarts. A single restart produces a curve with a knee that is not there.

## 4. Instrumentation and the calibration protocol

**Co-locate before deploying and after recovering.** Every low-cost unit spends at least two
weeks alongside the reference instrument before it goes out and at least one week on return.
This gives a per-device calibration and, from the difference between the two, a measured drift
rate. Without the closing co-location the drift is unbounded and the record cannot be corrected
retrospectively.

**Rotate one unit through the anchor continuously.** A single unit permanently at the reference
site provides an ongoing transfer standard, so a network-wide drift can be distinguished from a
change in the air.

**Log humidity with every measurement.** Low-cost optical sensors respond to hygroscopic growth,
and Kandy is humid for much of the year. A record without co-located humidity cannot be corrected
for it.

**Record mounting height, inlet exposure and distance to the nearest road edge at every site**,
because these are the variables the eventual analysis will need and they cannot be recovered
later from a photograph.

---

## 5. Temporal design

**Minimum twelve months.** Kandy's concentration has a strong seasonal structure with a March
maximum and a mid-year minimum, and the transboundary contribution is seasonal rather than
chronic. A campaign shorter than a year measures one season and generalises it.

**Include the March inter-monsoon peak and the mid-year monsoon minimum**, which bracket the
range. If the budget forces a shorter campaign, run two three-month windows at those extremes
rather than six continuous months in between.

**Hourly resolution or finer.** The diurnal cycle is bimodal, with a morning peak near 07, an
evening peak near 18 to 19, and the daily minimum at midday rather than at night. Daily means
destroy exactly the structure that distinguishes local traffic from regional background.

---

## 6. What this design would settle, ranked by how well it would settle it

**Definitely.** The level discrepancy, which needs only the anchor and three months. The
within-cell distribution at three locations, which needs the paired stratum and one month. What
eight named institutions are exposed to, which needs the receptor stratum and a year.

🔴 **NOT AT ALL, and this reverses what an earlier draft of this plan said.** Whether the spatial
ceiling is a sampling artefact or an information limit **cannot be settled by a campaign of this
size.** The detection limit was computed before deployment, as the registration required, and
`scripts/campaign_power.py` gives the answer: with **18** sites available to fit a spatial
pattern, beating the benchmark of 0.309 needs a gain of **+0.30 to +0.47**, against the **0.130**
the 46-city panel resolved. **Matching the panel in one city would need roughly 96 to 304 fitting
sites.**

The earlier draft rated this "probably" and flagged that the limit should be computed. Computing
it changed the answer. **The spatial test is demoted to exploratory before deployment**, reported
with its bound attached, and the campaign must not be proposed or written up as resolving the
spatial question. See `docs/prereg_kandy_campaign_2026-09-05.md` section 0.

**Not at all.** Source apportionment, which needs filter sampling and chemical analysis rather
than optical particle counters. The chemistry work of 2026-09-05 bounds the locally emitted
primary share only between 9.1 and 48.3 per cent, and **nothing in this design narrows that
range.** A speciation campaign is a separate proposal and should be costed as one.

---

## 7. What would falsify the premise

The design assumes deliberate siting breaks a ceiling that convenience siting could not. That
assumption is testable and the campaign tests it.

**If a deliberately contrasted 21-site network still yields a rank correlation near 0.2 to 0.3**,
the information-limited reading is confirmed far more strongly than six convenience-sample nulls
could confirm it, and the field gains a genuinely bounded statement about what kilometre-scale
products can do. **That is a good outcome, and it should be registered as such in advance** so it
cannot later be presented as a failed campaign.

**If it rises materially**, the ceiling was a sampling artefact, and this project's six nulls
have to be reread as a statement about network design rather than about the atmosphere.

Both outcomes are worth the money. A design that can only succeed is not an experiment.

---

## 8. What it costs, and the re-scope that turns out not to be worth doing

Generated by `scripts/campaign_costing.py`. Every unit price below is either cited to a public
source or left blank, and nothing is estimated.

### 8.1 Instruments

| line | quantity | unit USD | USD | source |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| low-cost outdoor monitors | 38 | 225 | 8,550 | vendor published price, AirGradient Open Air O-1PST |
| spares, 15 per cent | 6 | 225 | 1,350 | attrition and co-location rotation; a design choice |
| **low-cost subtotal, assembled** | **44** | | **9,900** | |
| the same as self-assembly kits | 44 | 125 | 5,500 | vendor published; saves 4,400 and costs assembly labour |
| reference-grade anchor | 1 | 10,000 to 40,000 | 10,000 to 40,000 | US EPA describes regulatory monitors as costing tens of thousands of dollars. **A range from a public statement, not a quote.** |
| **INSTRUMENT SUBTOTAL** | | | **19,900 to 49,900** | |

**Why AirGradient and not the cheapest available unit.** This project already holds per-device
calibration coefficients for AirGradient sensors, and its ingest pipeline already classifies
them. A different vendor means re-deriving a calibration that is in hand, which costs more than
the price difference. That is an argument from continuity, not from performance, and it should be
revisited if a local supplier changes the import position.

### 8.2 What is deliberately not costed

**Mounting and enclosures. Mains or solar power. Connectivity and data. Import duty and
clearance. Installation labour and transport. Twelve months of servicing. Co-location space for
calibration.**

None of these has a published unit price for Sri Lanka. Each appears here as a line item with an
empty price, which is what a procurement exercise fills in from local quotes. **A number typed
into any of them would be a guess wearing a budget's clothes**, and this document does not
contain one.

### 8.3 🔴 The largest line may not be a purchase at all

The reference anchor dominates the instrument budget, at between one and four times the entire
low-cost network. **It may cost a letter instead.**

The national environmental authority has already granted this project access in principle to a
Kandy regulatory station carrying hourly PM2.5, PM10, gases and full meteorology including a rain
gauge, subject to a formal agreement. If that route completes, C3 is answered without buying
anything and the instrument subtotal falls to the low-cost line alone, about 9,900 dollars.

**A campaign costed without pursuing that route first would overstate its own price by more than
the rest of the budget combined.** Securing the agreement is therefore not merely the first
scientific step, it is the largest single cost decision in the proposal.

### 8.4 The re-scope, and why it is not worth doing

Section 6 demoted the spatial hypothesis, which was the design stratum's main justification. That
raised a fair question: is a 12-site design stratum still worth buying?

The saturation curve answers it, and the answer is that this is not a cost problem.

| design sites | representativeness | change from 12 | saved | verdict |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 12 | 0.1297 | -- | -- | the registered design |
| 10 | 0.1292 | -0.0005 | 450 | **indistinguishable from 12** |
| 8 | 0.1401 | +0.0104 | 900 | a real but small loss, 8 per cent |
| 6 | 0.1673 | +0.0376 | 1,350 | **a cliff, 29 per cent. Do not.** |

**Cutting the stratum from 12 sites to 10 saves 450 dollars**, which is under three per cent of
the low-end instrument subtotal and about one per cent of the high end. The stratum is not where
the money is. At 225 dollars a unit, no plausible re-scoping of a low-cost network changes the
shape of this budget; the anchor does, and section 8.3 is the lever that matters.

**Recommendation: keep the stratum, at 10 or 12 sites indifferently, and spend the effort on the
agreement in section 8.3 rather than on trimming sensors.**

⚠ **This does not void the registration.** The design stratum serves the exploratory spatial
hypothesis, which the registration already carries as exploratory, and the void conditions in its
section 5 concern the paired triplets, the usable nights and the anchor. A change here is
reported as a dated deviation, which is what the registration asks for.

---

## 9. The three tensions, resolved

An earlier reading of this plan left three questions open. Each is answered here rather than left
for a reader to find.

### 9.1 The design stratum lost its justification when the spatial hypothesis was demoted

**Partly true, and it does not change what to buy.** The stratum was justified almost entirely by
the hypothesis that deliberate siting could break the spatial ceiling, and that hypothesis is now
exploratory. Two justifications survive and one is new.

It still serves the exploratory spatial test, reported with its bound.

**And it makes Kandy the only deliberately sited city in a 48-city panel of convenience samples.**
Every city in the frame that produced this project's spatial nulls was sited for compliance and
access. A single city sited for contrast is a different kind of data point, and it is worth more
to the multi-city frame than to Kandy. That is a real justification, arrived at after the
original one failed, and it is stated as such rather than presented as the plan's intent all
along.

Section 8.4 then shows the question is moot on cost grounds: the stratum is a 450-dollar
decision inside a 20,000-dollar budget.

### 9.2 The site count was set by saturation, which is not a power criterion

**True, and the number was over-precise.** Representativeness saturates and statistical power are
different quantities answering different questions, and the plan used the first to set a number
while the second had opinions about it.

The honest statement is narrower than the one the figure carries. **Ten sites and twelve sites
differ by 0.0005 in representativeness against a seed-to-seed standard deviation of 0.0092**, so
they are indistinguishable, and specifying one rather than the other is not supported by the
curve. The saturation point is a range of 10 to 12, not a value of 12.

The figure's single dashed line at 12 is therefore over-precise and is corrected to a band.

### 9.3 The best-powered test rests on one 2008 measurement of a different pollutant

**True, and the test is robust to it anyway**, which is the part that matters.

The concern is real: the 27.5-fold within-cell contrast comes from a single roadside survey of
PM10 conducted in 2004 to 2006, while the model delivers PM2.5. If that figure is wrong, the
expected effect size is wrong.

But the decision rule does not use it. C1 is held if the observed within-triplet ratio exceeds
**the model's own prediction of 1.58** by more than the measurement resolution, which is a factor
of 1.044 after seven days. The 27.5 figure tells us only that the test is likely to be decisive
rather than marginal. **If the true ratio is 3, or 5, or 10, C1 still resolves it comfortably.**

The test becomes marginal only if the true within-cell ratio sits within about 0.04 of the
model's 1.58, and that outcome would itself be the finding: it would mean the model's fine
surface is right about within-cell contrast, which nothing currently suggests and which would be
worth knowing.

---

## 10. Sequencing, and what to do first

**Phase 0, no equipment.** Register the analysis: the benchmark, the detection limit at 21 sites,
and the decision rule, all before deployment. The project's own record is that a null without a
stated detection limit converts a limitation of the experiment into a claim about the world, and
it cost four months once already.

**Phase 1, the anchor alone.** Secure the reference instrument. It settles the level discrepancy
on its own and every later phase depends on it. This is a letter and an agreement rather than a
purchase, and it is the long-lead item.

**Phase 2, the paired stratum.** Nine units, three locations, one month. The cheapest stratum,
the largest expected effect, and it can run before the design stratum is sited.

**Phase 3, the design and receptor strata.** Twenty units for twelve months.

**Phase 4, mobile augmentation if funds remain.** One or two units rotated through additional
locations on a fixed schedule, which extends coverage without extending the fixed network. Note
that a rotating unit measures different places at different times, so it informs the spatial mean
and not the temporal correlation, and it still needs the anchor.

---

## 11. Risks, stated so they can be planned for

**Siting failure.** Every coordinate here is a design, not a siting decision. Some will have no
power, no secure mounting, or an obstructed inlet. **The rule when a site fails a ground visit is
to move to the nearest cell in the same covariate stratum**, not to the nearest convenient
building, because the latter reintroduces exactly the convenience sampling the design exists to
remove. The generating script can supply the next-best candidate per stratum.

**Loss and theft.** Assume attrition. A design that only works at 30 of 30 sites is fragile;
this one degrades gracefully because the strata are separable, and the paired stratum is the one
to protect first since it has the largest expected effect per unit.

**Calibration drift** is handled by the closing co-location, and a unit recovered without one
should have its later record flagged rather than corrected by assumption.

**Over-reading a short record.** A campaign that runs through one season and reports an annual
figure repeats an error this project has already documented in its own extension tier, where
every aggregate diagnostic passed while the episode tail was absent.

---

## 12. Honest limitations of this plan

The emission surface driving the design is a **proxy** built from road-network centrality, not a
measured source inventory, and the project has separately shown it misplaces sources that are
spatially decoupled from roads. **Kandy has such a source**: biomass burning is 14.1 per cent of
measured mass against traffic's 7.6 per cent, and it has no admissible remote proxy. A design
that stratifies on a traffic-derived surface will under-sample residential burning, and the
honest response is to add sites in residential areas on that ground rather than to pretend the
proxy covers it.

The receptor layer comes from OpenStreetMap, whose completeness varies and cannot be measured
from the data. **A missing school is invisible here.** The 150 receptors are a lower bound.

Outdoor workers are the most exposed group in the city and **are not in this design at all**,
because they have no fixed location. Reaching them requires personal or mobile sampling, which is
a different instrument and a different protocol. Their absence is a gap in the plan rather than a
judgement that they matter less.

And the design optimises what can be computed, which is coverage of a covariate space. It does
not optimise expected reduction in decision loss, which is what a formal value-of-information
placement would do and what the nearest published work in this area does. That would need a
stated decision problem, and this project has not specified one.
